{{Short description|Mathematical conjecture}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''André–Oort conjecture''' is a problem in [[Diophantine geometry]], a branch of [[number theory]], that can be seen as a [[Abelian variety|non-abelian]] analogue of the [[Arithmetic of abelian varieties#Manin–Mumford conjecture|Manin–Mumford conjecture]], which is now a theorem (proven in several different ways).  The conjecture concerns itself with a characterization of the [[Zariski closure]] of sets of special points in [[Shimura varieties]]. A special case of the conjecture was stated by [[Yves André]] in 1989,<ref>{{Citation | last1=André | first1=Yves | title=''G''-functions and geometry | series=Aspects of Mathematics | volume=E13 | publisher=Vieweg | year=1989}}.</ref> and a more general statement (albeit with a restriction on the type of the Shimura variety) was conjectured by [[Frans Oort]] in 1995.<ref>{{Citation | last1=Oort | first1=Frans | chapter=Canonical liftings and dense sets of CM points | title=Arithmetic Geometry | editor=Fabrizio Catanese | publisher=Cambridge University Press | place=Cambridge | year=1997}}.</ref>  The modern version is a natural generalization of these two conjectures.

==Statement==

The conjecture in its modern form states that each irreducible component of the [[Zariski closure]] of a set of special points in a [[Shimura variety]] is a special subvariety.

André's first version of the conjecture was just for one-dimensional irreducible components, while Oort proposed that it should be true for irreducible components of arbitrary dimension in the moduli space of [[Abelian variety#Polarisation and dual abelian variety|principally polarised]] [[Abelian variety|Abelian varieties]] of dimension ''g''. It seems that André was motivated by applications to transcendence theory while Oort by the analogy with the Manin-Mumford conjecture.

==Results==

Various results have been established towards the full conjecture by Ben Moonen, [[Yves André]], [[Andrei Yafaev]], [[Bas Edixhoven]], [[Laurent Clozel]], [[Bruno Klingler]], and [[Emmanuel Ullmo]], among others.  Some of these results were conditional upon the [[generalized Riemann hypothesis]] (GRH) being true.  In fact, the proof of the full conjecture under GRH was published by Bruno Klingler, Emmanuel Ullmo, and Andrei Yafaev in 2014 in the [[Annals of Mathematics]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Klingler|first1=Bruno|last2=Yafaev|first2=Andrei|date=2014-11-01|title=The André-Oort conjecture|url=https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2014/180-3/p02|journal=Annals of Mathematics|language=en|pages=867–925|arxiv=1209.0936|doi=10.4007/annals.2014.180.3.2|issn=0003-486X}}</ref> In 2006, [[Umberto Zannier]] and [[Jonathan Pila]] used techniques from [[o-minimal theory|o-minimal]] geometry and [[transcendental number theory]] to develop an approach to the Manin–Mumford–André–Oort type of problems.  In 2009, Jonathan Pila proved the André–Oort conjecture unconditionally for arbitrary products of [[modular curve]]s,<ref>{{Citation | last1=Pila | first1=Jonathan | title=Rational points of definable sets and results of André–Oort–Manin–Mumford type | journal=Int. Math. Res. Not. | number=13 | year=2009 | pages=2476–2507}}.</ref><ref>{{Citation | last1=Pila | first1=Jonathan | title=O-minimality and the André–Oort conjecture for '''C'''<sup>''n''</sup> | journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] | volume=173 | issue=3 | year=2011 | pages=1779–1840 | doi=10.4007/annals.2011.173.3.11| doi-access=free }}.</ref> a result which earned him the 2011 [[Clay Research Award]].<ref>[http://www.claymath.org/research_award/ Clay Research Award website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110626122056/http://www.claymath.org/research_award/ |date=2011-06-26 }}</ref>

[[Bruno Klingler]], [[Emmanuel Ullmo]], and [[Andrei Yafaev]] proved, in 2014, the functional transcendence result needed for the general Pila–Zannier approach, and Emmanuel Ullmo deduced from it a technical result needed for the induction step in the strategy. The remaining technical ingredient was the problem of bounding below the Galois degrees of special points.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}<ref name=“CanonicalHeights”/>

For the case of the [[Siegel modular form|Siegel modular variety]], this bound was deduced by [[Jacob Tsimerman]] in 2015 from the [[Colmez conjecture|averaged Colmez conjecture]] and the Masser–Wustholtz isogeny estimates. The averaged Colmez conjecture was proved by [[Xinyi Yuan]] and [[Shou-Wu Zhang]] and independently by Andreatta, Goren, Howard, and Madapusi-Pera.<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |title=February 2018 |issn=1088-9477 |volume=65 |issue=2 |year=2018 |page=191}}</ref>

In 2019–2020, Gal Biniyamini, Harry Schmidt, and Andrei Yafaev, building on previous work and ideas of Harry Schmidt on torsion points in tori and abelian varieties and Gal Biniyamini's point-counting results, formulated a conjecture on bounds of heights of special points and deduced from its validity the bounds for the Galois degrees of special points needed for the proof of the full André–Oort conjecture.<ref>{{cite arXiv| last1=Binyamini | first1=Gal | last2=Schmidt | first2=Harry | last3=Yafaev | first3=Andrei | title=Lower bounds for Galois orbits of special points on Shimura varieties: a point-counting approach | date=2021 | eprint=2104.05842 | page= | class=math.NT }}</ref>

In September 2021, [[Jonathan Pila]], Ananth Shankar, and [[Jacob Tsimerman]] claimed in a paper (featuring an appendix written by [[Hélène Esnault]] and Michael Groechenig) a proof of the Biniyamini–Schmidt–Yafaev height conjecture, thus completing the proof of the André–Oort conjecture using the Pila–Zannier strategy.<ref name=“CanonicalHeights”>{{cite arXiv |last1=Pila |first1=Jonathan |last2=Shankar |first2=Ananth |last3=Tsimerman |first3=Jacob |last4=Esnault |first4=Hélène |last5=Groechenig |first5=Michael |date=2021-09-17 |title=Canonical Heights on Shimura Varieties and the André-Oort Conjecture |class=math.NT |eprint=2109.08788}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sloman |first=Leila |date=2022-02-03 |title=Mathematicians Prove 30-Year-Old André-Oort Conjecture |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/mathematicians-prove-30-year-old-andre-oort-conjecture-20220203/ |access-date=2022-02-04 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref>

==Coleman–Oort conjecture==
A related conjecture that has two forms, equivalent if the André–Oort conjecture is assumed, is the '''Coleman–Oort conjecture'''. [[Robert F. Coleman|Robert Coleman]] conjectured that for sufficiently large ''g'', there are only finitely many smooth projective curves ''C'' of genus ''g'', such that the [[Jacobian variety]] ''J''(''C'') is an [[abelian variety of CM-type]]. Oort then conjectured that the [[Torelli locus]] – of the [[moduli space of abelian varieties of dimension g]] – has for sufficiently large ''g'' no special subvariety of dimension > 0 that intersects the image of the [[Torelli mapping]] in a dense open subset.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Carlson |first1=James |last2=Müller-Stach |first2=Stefan |last3=Peters |first3=Chris |title=Period Mappings and Period Domains |date=2017 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=9781108422628 |page=285 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XrYrDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA485 |language=en}}</ref>

==Generalizations==

The Manin–Mumford and André–Oort conjectures can be generalized in many directions, for example by relaxing the properties of points being "special" (and considering the so-called "unlikely locus" instead) or looking at more general  ambient varieties: abelian or semi-abelian schemes, mixed Shimura varieties, etc. These generalizations are colloquially known as the [[Zilber–Pink conjecture]]s because problems of this type were proposed by Richard Pink<ref>{{Citation | last1=Pink | first1=Richard | chapter=A combination of the conjectures of Mordell–Lang and André–Oort | title=Geometric methods in algebra and number theory | series=Progress in Mathematics | volume=253 | publisher=Birkhauser | year=2005 | pages=251–282}}.</ref> and [[Boris Zilber]].<ref>{{Citation | last1=Zilber | first1=Boris | title=Exponential sums equations and the Schanuel conjecture | journal=J. London Math. Soc. | number=2 | volume=65 | year=2002 | pages=27–44 | doi=10.1112/S0024610701002861}}.</ref><ref>{{Citation | last1=Rémond | first1=Gaël | title=Autour de la conjecture de Zilber–Pink | language=fr | journal=J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux | number=2 | volume=21 | year=2009 | pages=405–414 | doi=10.5802/jtnb.677| url=http://www.numdam.org/item/JTNB_2009__21_2_405_0/ | doi-access=free }}.</ref> Most of these questions are open and are a subject of current active research.
